trickyParts: A person's reply to a message is a message.answered event, so S1 and the 0121 index take message.answered as well as message.created.
Delivery rows' created_at can precede the item's own created_at by the writing transaction's length, so the window is applied to the item and the delivery arms are bounded an hour before it.
Oh My Pi drops everything a context handler returns when it throws, so the handler catches a failed list read: a list failure never costs the dispatch-first skill.
The claude hook resolves Dispatch with kept commands first and runs a `!` token command only in a worker thread it stops waiting on at 800 ms after process start.
readSessionAnswers treats a 200 whose body is no answers list as a failed read (the existing dispatch-first stand-in answers every path with the listener's JSON).
Claude Code starts every hook beside itself, so Bun's start-up can pass 800 ms; the hook's deadline is the later of 800 ms after process start and 150 ms after its code begins.

Routing a reply to the document's writers would deliver twice to a writer the reply mentions, because a reply's suppressed_authors held only the thread root's author; outside an ask thread it now names every mentioned session, as a new comment's does.
deviations: Census files are `select 0` with a comment, as 0082's is: a non-zero census refuses the deploy, so a row count would block every deploy.
owner and ref are null for a direct message, which has no issue and no dispatch:// address; its href is /agents/<session>/live.
Oh My Pi passes the context handler no abort signal, so the per-request read cannot be cancelled by the run's abort; Oh My Pi drops an aborted handler's result itself.
The real-binary Claude test calls the subagent tool `Agent` (Claude Code 2.1.311's API name for Task).
The real-provider cache proof ran at 1bf8a34e; later heads changed no placement code, and pi-envoy's real-binary case (h) passes at the merge 16ed9c87.

A hook whose Bun start-up takes longer than 650 ms can now run past 800 ms after process start, by at most 150 ms plus the 50 ms settle: the tester's red test requires the list Dispatch answers at once even after an 820 ms start-up.
discoveredComplexity: The answers-hook wall-time checks (< 1 s) measured 0.87-0.90 s on this loaded pod because Bun start-up varies 240-760 ms; a very loaded CI runner could make them flaky.
